Amberford bakery prepares new packing line for autumn commissioning

By Leonie Varnet

28 August 2026

Bramble Foods has completed the main installation work on a new packing line at its Amberford bakery. The KRN 8.4 million project replaces two older machines used for small cake packs and is scheduled to enter commissioning in October. Electrical checks and staff training will take place during September.

Once fully operational, the line is expected to increase the site's cake packing capacity by 18% and reduce film waste per pack by about 11%. These estimates will be checked during production trials. The bakery will continue supplying customers through its existing equipment while the new line is tested.

The project includes 14 additional permanent roles across production, maintenance and quality control. Recruitment has begun locally, with practical training provided on site. Bramble Foods said the investment supports demand for smaller packs without requiring an extension to the bakery building. Total spending remains within the approved project budget.

Amberford packing trials meet quality targets ahead of production

By Leonie Varnet

16 October 2026

Bramble Foods has completed the initial commissioning trials for its new cake packing line at Amberford. Trial packs met the site's checks for seal strength, weight accuracy and product protection. The line is scheduled to begin regular customer production on 19 October, initially operating on one shift.

The KRN 8.4 million investment was outlined in August. All 14 additional permanent roles have now been filled, and operators have completed supervised training. Existing packing equipment will remain available during the early production period so that the bakery can maintain deliveries if adjustments are required.

Early trials indicate that the line can support the planned increase in capacity, but Bramble Foods will assess sustained output and packaging waste over a full month of production. The company expects to add a second shift as orders require. Final project spending remains within budget, including installation, training and a supply of essential spare parts.

Bramble Foods agrees purchase of Val-Brume specialist bakery

By Mara Fenwick

18 September 2026

Bramble Foods has agreed to acquire Hearthmere Bakery, a privately owned producer of crispbreads and seeded biscuits based in Val-Brume, for KRN 24.6 million in cash. The purchase remains subject to competition clearance and customary completion conditions. Completion is expected by the end of October.

Hearthmere Bakery employs 86 people at a single production site in Kestria's French-speaking region. It recorded revenue of KRN 31.8 million in its last financial year. Its range would add specialist baked snacks to Bramble Foods' existing bakery and biscuit business.

Bramble Foods intends to retain the Hearthmere name, the Val-Brume site and its workforce. The proposed acquisition would be funded from existing cash and committed borrowing facilities. Until completion, both businesses will continue to operate independently. Bramble Foods has not included any contribution from Hearthmere in its current trading expectations and will provide a further announcement when the transaction completes.

Bramble Foods announces October price changes for selected snacks

By Tobin Vale

20 August 2026

Bramble Foods has notified retail customers of price increases averaging 2.5% across selected biscuits and savoury snacks, effective from 1 October 2026. The changes apply to wholesale list prices in Kestria. Standard sliced bread and plain bread rolls are excluded from this announcement.

The company said higher costs for edible oils, cocoa ingredients and flexible packaging had continued through the summer. Savings from purchasing and factory improvements have absorbed part of those increases. Individual product changes will vary, and retailers will decide the prices paid by shoppers.

Bramble Foods is giving customers six weeks to update ordering systems and review planned promotions. Existing promotional agreements covering September will be honoured. Customer teams based in Saltmarsh and Kestrel Bay will provide revised price lists and product details directly to retailers. Pack weights and recipes will remain unchanged as part of this price review.

Bramble Foods completes acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery in Val-Brume

By Mara Fenwick

21 October 2026

Bramble Foods today completed its acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery for KRN 24.6 million in cash. All remaining completion conditions have been satisfied following competition clearance announced on 9 October. Hearthmere's financial results will be included in Bramble Foods' group accounts from today.

The Val-Brume business makes crispbreads and seeded biscuits and employs 86 people. Its name, production site and workforce have been retained. Customers will continue to place orders through their existing contacts, and current supply agreements remain in effect. Product recipes and packaging are unchanged at completion.

The purchase was funded through a combination of available cash and drawings under Bramble Foods' existing borrowing facilities. During the first three months of ownership, work will concentrate on reporting systems, supplier arrangements and planning for future orders. Bramble Foods expects a small contribution to group revenue for the remainder of 2026 and will provide further detail with its full-year results.

Bramble Foods pays interim dividend of twelve crowns cents

By Mara Fenwick

30 September 2026

Bramble Foods today paid its interim dividend of KRN 0.12 per ordinary share to shareholders who were on the register on 4 September 2026. The payment follows the dividend declaration included in the company's half-year results on 17 August. The total distribution is KRN 7.2 million.

Shareholders receiving payment by bank transfer should allow for their bank's normal processing times. Those who have elected to receive paper payment notices will receive them at their registered address. Dividend statements are also available through the company's shareholder account service.

Investors who have recently changed their address or bank details should check that their shareholder records are current. Bramble Foods' investor relations team in Saltmarsh can explain how to submit updates securely. The company will issue its next scheduled trading update on 19 October, covering revenue and trading conditions for the three months ended 30 September.

Bramble Foods reports higher first half sales and operating profit

By Mara Fenwick

17 August 2026

Bramble Foods, the listed Kestrian bakery and snacks company, today reported revenue of KRN 428.6 million for the six months ended 30 June 2026, up 6.4% on the same period last year. Operating profit rose to KRN 34.2 million from KRN 30.8 million. Sales volumes increased by 2.1%, with the remaining revenue growth coming from prices and changes in the mix of products sold.

Packaged bread performed steadily, while savoury crackers and small cake packs recorded stronger growth. Lower waste at the Amberford bakery helped offset higher flour and packaging costs. Net debt at the period end was KRN 76.5 million, compared with KRN 81.3 million a year earlier.

The board declared an interim dividend of KRN 0.12 per share, payable on 30 September to shareholders registered on 4 September. Bramble Foods continues to expect modest volume growth during the second half, although household spending remains uneven across Kestria.

Competition clearance received for proposed Hearthmere Bakery acquisition

By Mara Fenwick

9 October 2026

Bramble Foods has received clearance from Kestria's competition authority for its proposed acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery. The KRN 24.6 million cash transaction was announced on 18 September. Clearance satisfies one of the principal conditions of the purchase agreement, with completion still subject to the remaining customary requirements.

The companies are now preparing final completion documents and arrangements for transferring ownership. Bramble Foods continues to expect the transaction to complete by the end of October. Hearthmere remains independently owned and managed until that process has concluded.

Plans announced in September to retain Hearthmere's name, Val-Brume production site and 86 employees remain in place. Initial work following completion would focus on financial reporting, purchasing procedures and customer service arrangements. Bramble Foods said there would be no immediate changes to Hearthmere's recipes or product packaging. A separate announcement will confirm completion and the date from which Hearthmere's results enter the group accounts.

Kestrel Bay bakery completes oven heat recovery installation

By Leonie Varnet

20 October 2026

Bramble Foods has brought a new heat recovery system into service at its Kestrel Bay bakery following installation during planned maintenance. The KRN 1.3 million system captures heat from oven exhausts and uses it to warm water for cleaning. It serves two bread ovens at the site.

Engineering estimates suggest the equipment could reduce the bakery's annual purchased energy use by around 6%. Actual savings will depend on production hours and seasonal demand for hot water. Bramble Foods will compare meter readings with production volumes over the next six months before reporting a measured result.

Installation took place over three scheduled maintenance weekends, with bread deliveries maintained from existing stocks and production at other group bakeries. Maintenance staff have received training on cleaning and inspection requirements. The project forms part of the company's approved factory investment programme and does not change the site's production capacity or staffing levels.

New oat cracker range reaches Kestrian shops this month

By Tobin Vale

23 September 2026

Bramble Foods will begin supplying its new Bramble Table oat crackers to retailers on 28 September. The range comprises plain oat, toasted onion and garden herb varieties in 180 gram packs. Distribution will start in Saltmarsh and Ostara before extending to other parts of Kestria during October.

The crackers are made at the company's Ostara snacks plant using an existing baking line adapted during the summer. Bramble Foods has invested KRN 620,000 in mixing equipment and product development. The recommended retail price is KRN 2.80 per pack, although individual retailers will set their own selling prices.

Development included tasting sessions with 240 adult volunteers and checks on breakage during transport. The company has arranged an initial eight-week production programme, with later output dependent on repeat orders. Ingredient and allergen information will appear on every pack, alongside storage guidance intended to help customers keep opened crackers fresh.

October snack price changes take effect across customer orders

By Tobin Vale

5 October 2026

Bramble Foods has implemented the wholesale price changes announced on 20 August. Revised prices took effect on 1 October for selected biscuits and savoury snacks, with an average increase of 2.5% across the affected range. Standard sliced bread and plain bread rolls remain outside this review.

The company's customer service teams checked the first orders under the revised lists last week. A small number of invoice queries are being resolved directly with retailers. Deliveries have continued to schedule, and no product withdrawals or changes to pack weights have accompanied the price adjustment.

Bramble Foods said the increase addresses part of the higher ingredient and packaging costs reported during the summer. Retailers continue to set their own shelf prices and promotional offers. The company will monitor order patterns over the coming weeks, recognising that a few days of trading cannot establish how shoppers will respond to any resulting shelf price changes.

Third quarter sales rise as bakery demand remains steady

By Mara Fenwick

19 October 2026

Bramble Foods recorded revenue of KRN 219.4 million for the three months ended 30 September 2026, an increase of 4.8% compared with the same quarter last year. Revenue for the first nine months reached KRN 648.0 million. Third-quarter sales volumes grew by 1.3%, supported by steady bread demand and higher cracker sales.

Trading remained strongest in Saltmarsh and Amberford, while orders from smaller shops were more variable. The new oat cracker range began shipping near the quarter end and made only a small contribution. Wholesale price changes introduced on 1 October had no effect on the reported quarter.

The board's full-year operating profit expectations remain unchanged. Regular production on Amberford's new packing line began today, with performance monitoring under way. The proposed Hearthmere Bakery acquisition has received competition clearance but has not yet completed. Its trading is therefore excluded from these figures, and completion remains expected by the end of October.
